name: TestGorilla
summary: Pre-employment skills testing: assessment library, custom questions and candidate scoring.
best_for: companies that screen enough candidates to use a credit pool every month, and who will use the 350+ test library rather than writing their own questions
skip_if: you hire a handful of people a year and only need one simple test: the free tier plus a well-designed take-home task covers occasional hiring
honest_knock: The Assessments bill is set by credits, and the page does not say how many credits its 'from' prices include. Core starts from $77 a month billed annually or from $287 billed monthly; that gap is far wider than the 25% annual saving the page advertises, so the two floors are different allowances. An AI interview costs 2 credits a candidate and a skills test 1, so the real price depends on how you build each assessment and how many people you invite. Get the credit allowance in writing before you compare it with a per-seat tool.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-07 in a browser render of testgorilla.com/pricing with the currency set to USD; the page defaults to euros from a European connection; re-verified unchanged 2026-10-15 on both billing toggles) TestGorilla now sells two products that you can buy on their own or together. Gorilla Sourcing, a candidate-search product priced per Sourcing seat: Free $0 (browse and preview only, no invites); Core $74 a month per seat billed annually or $99 billed monthly, with 500 invites per seat a month and 1 seat; Plus $134 a month per seat billed annually or $179 billed monthly, with 1,500 invites per seat a month and up to 5 seats. Gorilla Assessments, the skills-testing product, priced per account: Free $0 with 10 credits a month (5 essential tests with unlimited use, 180+ tests with limited use, 5 preset custom questions, 1 premium user role); Core from $77 a month billed annually or from $287 billed monthly, with the full library of 350+ tests, a shared account-wide credit pool and 2 premium user roles; Plus from $520 a month billed annually or from $694 billed monthly, adding the AI interview library, custom AI interviews, job simulations, custom tests and coding challenges, ID verification, ATS and API integrations and unlimited premium roles. Annual billing is advertised as saving 25%. Credits: resume scoring and qualifying questions cost nothing; a premium skills test, a video question or an ID check costs 1 credit per candidate; an AI interview or a job simulation costs 2. The page does not say how many credits each 'from' price includes.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested TestGorilla on Free plans that we created. An assessment for a made-up Customer Support Agent, with the tests Communication, Problem Solving and Email Skills (Gmail), was ready about 3 minutes after the onboarding was opened (3 onboarding screens, 4 build steps, about 25 clicks and entries); nobody was invited, so no candidate round and no score report were run. The Free plan showed 10 credits a month and the paid plans were read in the app and on the pricing page: the from amount of Assessments Core differs per view (from $215 in the text of the page, EUR 66 for 250 credits a year in the app and in the rendered page), and neither the $77 nor the $287 of our dossier was seen, so this is recorded as a vendor update dated 19 Nov 2026. The payment details of Core (EUR 2,220 for a year, renewing automatically) were seen and closed with no card. Account and start: we created the account and set the password, so the sign-up does not count in the times, and our AI assistant ran the test in its own tab of our browser. The onboarding was opened at 08:48 on 19 November 2026; the interface was already in English. The plans were Assessment Free and Sourcing Free. The dossier name is TestGorilla and the review is on OSM (osm/testgorilla-review.html). The made-up job and data were Test Recruiter, Test Company and Customer Support Agent for a small online shop. Onboarding: step 1 Tell us more about yourself (first name, last name and a phone number; the three boxes for marketing, SMS and WhatsApp stayed empty and no SMS code came), step 2 Tell us about your company (company name, 1-15 employees, role Recruiter), step 3 Where do you want to start? with Gorilla Sourcing (Find candidates) or Gorilla Assessments (Assess candidates); we chose Assess candidates. No link with an ATS, Google or LinkedIn was asked. The start screen said Hi Test!, Free plan active, Includes 10 credits per month and a checklist Jumpstart hiring at 20%. No card was asked during the whole sign-up. Core action, an assessment in four steps: (1) Job details, the question What role are you hiring for? and the language English, filled with Customer Support Agent for a small online shop and the skills written English, problem solving and attention to detail. (2) Tools (0/8): Qualifying questions Free, ID verification Upgrade, Skills tests 0-1 credit, Custom questions Free, AI interviews 2 credits, Video questions 1 credit, Resume scoring Free and Job simulations Upgrade; we chose Skills tests. (3) Content: Essentials, unlimited on your plan, with five tests (Big 5 (OCEAN), Communication, Problem Solving, Motivation and Time Management), with the line Your Free plan includes 5 essential tests you can use with unlimited candidates, no credits needed. We chose Communication (8 mins) and Problem Solving (9 mins), and from the Included test suggestions, which cost 1 credit per candidate from the 10 monthly free credits, Email Skills (Gmail), 1 credit, 10 mins, 16 questions. The total said 3 added, 27 mins. Other suggestions were Email Skills (Microsoft Outlook), Salesforce CRM and Verbal Reasoning, each 1 credit. (4) Settings: Job invitation details; Manage team access, Intro/Outro Video and Deadline and expiration date all say Upgrade required. Anti-cheating is on by default: a webcam photo every 15 seconds, an AI analysis of the photos and Candidates must use a single screen, with the lines Consumes 1 credit per candidate from your free monthly allocation and 1 free credit per candidate. The button Finalize ended it. After Finalize the job page New job, 19 November 2026 with the label Draft showed the cards Invite candidates, Try your assessment and Find candidates for this job, and the tabs Candidates, Assessment tools, Analytics, Job details and Settings. Time: from the onboarding at 08:48 to Finalize at 08:50 it took about 3 minutes, with 3 onboarding screens, 4 build steps and about 25 clicks and entries. Candidate view and plans: the eye icon in the builder opens an Assessment preview with sample questions only (tabs Communication, Problem Solving and Email Skills (Gmail)); nobody was invited and no mail was sent. Try your assessment and Invite were not used, because they send an invitation to an address, so there was no own candidate round and no score report. Account, Plan & billing shows Assessment Free, 10 credits/month, refreshes monthly, 10 credits remaining, 0 of 10 credits used and Next reset: Dec 1; Sourcing Free has no contact credits and contacting and opening up candidates starts on Sourcing Core. A credit is 1 per candidate for a premium test, so our assessment costs 1 credit per candidate and 10 candidates a month fit in the free credits; this was read, not run. Plans: In the app (Upgrade, Pricing plans window, currency EUR, switch Pay monthly or Pay annually with SAVE 25%): Gorilla Sourcing, annually, Free EUR 0 (0 invites, browse and preview only), Core EUR 64 per Sourcing seat per month and Plus EUR 116; monthly Core EUR 85 and Plus EUR 154. Gorilla Assessments, annually, Free EUR 0 (10 credits/mo), Core from EUR 66 per month and Plus from EUR 345 per month. Core has a list: 250 credits/year at EUR 66 per month (EUR 792 billed annually), 450 credits/year at EUR 115 (EUR 1,380 billed annually) and 750 credits/year at EUR 185 (EUR 2,220 billed annually), all pooled for the year. With the switch on Pay monthly, Assessments shows no price, only Free Assessments included: 10 credits a month and the line to switch to Pay annually to see the offering. On the public pricing page (USD, text read while loading): Sourcing Free $0, Core $74 per seat and Plus $134 per seat, billed annually; Assessments Free $0 (10 credits per month, refreshes monthly), Core from $215 per month and Plus from $520 per month, billed annually, SAVE 25%. When the same page was shown in the browser it showed the same cards in euros, Core from EUR 66 and Plus from EUR 345, so the from amount of Core differs per view ($215 in the text, EUR 66 in the app and in the rendered page). Credits on the pricing page: skills tests (350+ premium) 1 credit per candidate, video questions 1 credit per candidate, AI interviews 2 credits per candidate (Plus), job simulations 2 credits (Plus), ID verification 1 credit (Plus). Free: 5 essentials with unlimited use and no credits, 180+ limited tests at 1 Free plan credit per candidate, 5 preset custom questions, 1 premium user role. Core: the full test library of 350+ tests, a shared account-wide credit pool and 2 premium user roles. Plus: the full AI interviews library of 100+, ATS and API integrations, removal of the TestGorilla branding and unlimited premium user roles. The dossier says Core from $77 a month billed annually and from $287 billed monthly; neither amount was seen now (the page text says from $215, the app says EUR 66 for 250 credits a year, and Assessments has no monthly price in the app). This is recorded as a vendor update dated 19 Nov 2026, not as a correction of the dossier. Checkout: Get started at Assessments Core opened Payment details with Assessment Core (750 credits) EUR 2,220/year, Total due today EUR 2,220 (EUR), the line that the subscription renews automatically on November 19th, 2027, the box I agree to the Terms and Conditions and understand my Core subscription remains annual, and a saved Link payment method. Nothing was filled in and nothing was clicked except the cross to close it. No image of this screen was kept, because it shows a payment method. Cancelling: a free plan has nothing to cancel. Account, Plan & billing shows Manage plan and Upgrade now for both products; Manage plan was not opened. Account, My profile has only Switch account (Leave this account to join another) and no button to delete the account. The cancelling route of the paid annual Core plan was not seen. Not tested: inviting a candidate, finishing the test yourself and the score report; Try your assessment and Invite; writing an own custom question; Gorilla Sourcing (search, 900M profiles); Plus features, ATS links, Manage plan and the monthly prices of Assessments (not shown in the app); what one candidate really costs in credits. Clean up: the account, the draft job New job, 19 November 2026 (job id and assessment id in the note) and the test data stay; no candidate, no mail and no payment; the own tab was closed and our other tabs, including a TestGorilla tab on the onboarding address, were not touched. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The from price of Assessments Core is not the same in every view: from $215 in the text of the pricing page, EUR 66 in the app and in the rendered page, and the monthly price of Assessments is not shown at all in the app. Core is annual only, and what the 250 credits a year buy per candidate is only clear from the line 1 credit per candidate. Settings, the anti-cheating options (a webcam photo every 15 seconds and one screen) are on by default and use a credit per candidate. There is no button to delete the account in My profile.
